title: Toute la famille est là  (The Whole Family's Here)

segments.t: At the tribute, Camille asks Hippolyte about running through the cemetery. Then his mother Catherine joins them. Camille is about to discover that Mathias is Hippolyte's father as well as her own. Catherine knows Camille only as the agency's new assistant. Listen first as the introductions reveal the family connection.
Oui, j'ai couru dans le cimetière.
Voici Catherine, ma mère.
Bonjour, madame.
Voici Camille, la nouvelle assistante d'Andréa.
Mon mari a travaillé avec Samuel pendant quinze ans.
Quand on parle du loup… Mathias!
Camille est l'assistante d'Andréa.
Oui, Hippolyte me l'a dit.
Je ne savais pas que votre fils était acteur.
Pourquoi tu ne m'as pas dit ça?
Qu'est-ce que ça change?
J'ai soif.
On va prendre un verre?
Let's take it slowly. Hippolyte answers Camille's question about running through the cemetery, before his mother joins them.
Oui, j'ai couru dans le cimetière.
'Yes, I ran in the cemetery.' Have plus run places the action in the past. In the cemetery gives the location. Hippolyte repeats Camille's wording as he answers her question.
Voici Catherine, ma mère.
'This is Catherine, my mother.' The first word is the one you use to present someone: 'here is'. Camille greets her politely.
Bonjour, madame.
'Hello, madam.' The second word is a respectful way to address a woman. It adds politeness to the greeting without using a word for you. Catherine and Camille have just been introduced.
Voici Camille, la nouvelle assistante d'Andréa.
'This is Camille, Andréa's new assistant.' To say whose assistant, French says 'the assistant of Andréa'. There's no apostrophe-s. Then a bit of family history.
Mon mari a travaillé avec Samuel pendant quinze ans.
'My husband worked with Samuel for fifteen years.' Husband names Catherine's relationship to Mathias. For introduces the length of time they worked together, while with names his colleague, Samuel.
Quand on parle du loup… Mathias!

'Speak of the devil… Mathias!' The French saying literally means when you speak of the wolf. Catherine has just mentioned her husband when he appears. He remarks that the whole family is now here. His arrival makes Camille realise who Hippolyte's father is.
Camille est l'assistante d'Andréa.
'Camille is Andréa's assistant.' Again, 'the assistant of Andréa'. Mathias plays it cool.
Oui, Hippolyte me l'a dit.
'Yes, Hippolyte told me.' Catherine answers Camille. Told it to me is packed into the short French past: me identifies the person informed, and it refers to Camille's job at the agency.
Je ne savais pas que votre fils était acteur.

'I didn't know your son was an actor.' Camille addresses Catherine politely with your son. Knew describes her earlier lack of knowledge; was an actor names the job without needing a word for an before actor in French.
Pourquoi tu ne m'as pas dit ça?

'Why didn't you tell me that?' Camille now turns to Hippolyte and uses familiar you. The negative surrounds the past helper, while me comes before it. Her question asks why he kept the family connection from her.
Qu'est-ce que ça change?

'What difference does it make?' Literally what does that change? That stands for the fact they have just discussed. For Hippolyte it seems unimportant, while Camille understands that they share a father.
J'ai soif.
'I'm thirsty.' In French you don't 'are' thirsty, you 'have' thirst. It's her way of escaping the conversation.
On va prendre un verre?

'Shall we get a drink?' Literally 'we're going to take a glass?'. The verb 'to go' plus another verb talks about the near future. Now listen to the whole scene again. Now listen to the whole scene again.
Oui, j'ai couru dans le cimetière.
Voici Catherine, ma mère.
Bonjour, madame.
Voici Camille, la nouvelle assistante d'Andréa.
Mon mari a travaillé avec Samuel pendant quinze ans.
Quand on parle du loup… Mathias!
Camille est l'assistante d'Andréa.
Oui, Hippolyte me l'a dit.
Je ne savais pas que votre fils était acteur.
Pourquoi tu ne m'as pas dit ça?
Qu'est-ce que ça change?
J'ai soif.
On va prendre un verre?

Camille now knows that the man she kissed is her half-brother. Catherine still sees an ordinary introduction at an agency gathering. Listen again for the family words and the simple statement of thirst that lets Camille escape the conversation. See you next time!
Salut!
